rationale.Physical Exam: Abdomen: Courvoisier's sign: palpable non-tender gallbladder in jaundiced patient. RUQ mass.
rationale.BMP / CMP / LFTs: Obstructive pattern: elevated ALP, GGT, direct bilirubin. AST/ALT mildly elevated.
rationale.CA 19-9: Tumor marker. Prognostic + monitors treatment response. Not diagnostic (false positives in cholangitis, pancreatitis).
rationale.CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast (panc: Dual-phase CT for pancreatic mass, vascular involvement, liver mets. Most important staging study.
rationale.EUS with FNA: Tissue diagnosis. Endoscopic ultrasound with fine needle aspiration of pancreatic mass.
rationale.ERCP / MRCP: Imaging of biliary tree. Therapeutic: biliary stent if obstruction.
rationale.Consult, oncology / Surgical oncology: Multidisciplinary decision: resectable (Whipple) vs palliative chemotherapy.
rationale.Refer to palliative care: Pancreatic cancer has poor prognosis — early palliative care improves QOL.
rationale.MRI as first-line for pancreatic mass: CT with pancreatic protocol (dual-phase, IV contrast) is first-line. MRI is second-line when CT is equivocal or patient cannot receive contrast.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with painless jaundice, dark urine, clay-colored stools, pruritus, and weight loss — classic for malignant biliary obstruction. Courvoisier's sign: palpable, non-tender gallbladder in a jaundiced patient = malignancy until proven otherwise (most commonly pancreatic head adenocarcinoma). Pancreatic cancer most commonly arises in the head of the pancreas (70%), causing early obstructive jaundice. Late presentation is the rule — most are unresectable at diagnosis. Workup: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast (pancreatic protocol — dual-phase) for staging. CA 19-9 tumor marker (not diagnostic but prognostic and monitors recurrence). ERCP/MRCP for biliary drainage if needed. Biopsy via EUS-FNA. If resectable (localized, no vascular involvement, no mets): pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure). If unresectable: palliative biliary stenting, chemotherapy (gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel or FOLFIRINOX). Poor prognosis — 5-year survival <10%.
